definition_zh: 租金；租用；出租
definition_en: money paid regularly for the use of a house, room, or land, or the act of paying to use something
core_image: 每个月把一叠钱交到房东手里，换来一扇可以安心关上的门
scene: 月底房东来收钱，年轻人把房租转过去，钥匙仍在自己口袋里。 At the end of the month she paid the rent and kept the key to her small flat.
sceneCN: 这里 rent 是「租金」（第 1 个义项：为使用房屋或土地而定期支付的钱）；句意：月底她付了房租，继续拿着小公寓的钥匙。

derivatives.zh: 租金收入；租赁
租户
可出租的

senses.title: Money paid to use a home
senses.definition: money that you pay regularly to the owner of a house, room, or piece of land so that you can use it
senses.definitionCN: 为使用房屋、房间或土地而定期支付给所有者的钱
senses.example: The rent is due on the first day of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 房租在每月第一天到期。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the word is a regular payment returned to a landlord, so the money itself comes first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的义项就是定期交给房东的款项，所以「钱」本身是最核心的一层。

senses.title: To pay for the use of something
senses.definition: to pay money to use a house, car, or other thing that belongs to someone else
senses.definitionCN: 付钱使用属于别人的房屋、汽车或其他东西
senses.example: They rented a small flat near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站附近租了一间小公寓。
senses.why: Once the payment has a name, the act of making that payment naturally takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然这笔款项有了名称，做出支付行为的动作也就自然沿用了同一个词。

senses.title: To let someone use for payment
senses.definition: to allow someone to use your property in return for money
senses.definitionCN: 允许别人使用你的财物并收取费用
senses.example: She rents out the spare room to students.
senses.exampleCN: 她把空房间出租给学生。
senses.why: The same transaction looks different from the owner's side, so the verb also means to let out.
senses.whyCN: 同一笔交易从房东的角度看是另一回事，所以动词也引申为「出租」。

intro.en: Rent goes back through French to Latin reddita, a word for things given back, especially money owed to a landlord.
intro.cn: rent 经由法语上溯到拉丁语 reddita，指「交还之物」，尤指欠房东的钱。

items.en: Reddere means to give back, and it is built from red-, back, and dare, to give.
items.cn: reddere 意为交还，由 red-（回）与 dare（给）构成。

items.en: Reddita, its feminine participle, names payments or returns that are owed to an owner.
items.cn: 其阴性分词 reddita 指应当交还给所有者的款项或回报。

items.en: Renta appears in medieval records as a regular income drawn from property.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 renta 出现在记录中，指从地产获得的定期收入。

items.en: Old French rente means a yearly income or the money paid for the use of land.
items.cn: 古法语 rente 指年金，或为使用土地而支付的钱。

items.en: Anglo-Norman legal texts bring rente into English property law.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼法律文书把 rente 带入英语的财产法。

items.en: Middle English rent names both the payment and the holding that produces it.
items.cn: 中古英语 rent 既指这笔款项，也指产生这笔款项的租用地。

note.en: Rent sits in a family of payment and tenancy words, and it is easily confused with the unrelated verb rend.
note.cn: rent 属于「付款与租住」词族，同时容易与毫不相干的动词 rend 混淆。

entries.definition: the money paid or received for the use of property
a person who pays rent to live somewhere
to tear something violently
entries.definitionCN: 撕裂；扯破，与 rent 拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a legal agreement to use property for a fixed period
to pay to use something for a short time
a person who rents a place to live

normalIntro.en: Rent is a payment word, so the hooks link its letters and sound to money handed over for a place to stay.
normalIntro.cn: rent 是一个「付款」词，所以记忆钩子把它的字母和读音同「为住处交钱」联系起来。

normal.en: The first letter r can stand for regular: a regular payment for a room.
normal.cn: 首字母 r 可以代表 regular：为房间定期支付的款项。

normal.en: Rent and renter share a stem, so the person and the payment stay together.
normal.cn: rent 与 renter 共享词干，付款的人和款项绑在一起记。

normal.en: Compare rental: the ending -al turns the payment into the business of letting.
normal.cn: 对比 rental：词尾 -al 把款项变成「租赁业」。

normal.en: Rent out reverses the direction: the owner receives instead of pays.
normal.cn: rent out 把方向倒过来：房东是收钱而不是付钱。

normal.en: The phrase for rent is what you see on a sign in an empty window.
normal.cn: for rent 就是空窗上挂着的招租字样。

abstract.en: Picture a key handed over only after a folded note passes the other way.
abstract.cn: 想象一张叠好的钞票先递过去，钥匙才被交到手里。

abstract.en: Imagine a calendar with the first day of every month circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上每月第一天都被红笔圈起来。

abstract.en: Think of a landlord's receipt book filling with identical stubs.
abstract.cn: 想象房东的收据本一页页填满相同的存根。

examples.en: The rent for the flat includes water and electricity.
examples.cn: 这套公寓的租金包含水电费。

examples.en: He rented a bike for the afternoon.
examples.cn: 他租了一辆自行车用一个下午。

examples.en: They rent out their garage to a neighbour.
examples.cn: 他们把车库出租给邻居。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「润特」——把房子打理得润泽舒适，要特别付一笔钱；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 reddere（交还）的分词 reddita（应交之物）→ 古法语 rente（定期收入）→ 中古英语 rent，指为使用土地或房屋而定期支付的款项。

sensesIntro.en: One payment returns every month: first the money itself, then the tenant's act of paying, then the owner's act of letting.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一笔款项每月返回一次：先是钱本身，再是租客付款的动作，最后是房东出租的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded payment passed to the owner each month for the right to stay.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个月把一笔钱交给房主，换取继续住下去的权利。

branches.en: The regular payment itself is the first and oldest sense.
branches.cn: 定期支付的款项本身，是最早、最核心的义项。

branches.en: Paying that money becomes the tenant's verb.
branches.cn: 支付这笔钱，成为租客一方的动词。

branches.en: Receiving that money becomes the owner's verb.
branches.cn: 收取这笔钱，成为房东一方的动词。

branches.en: The payment and the paying are two sides of one monthly act.
branches.cn: 款项与付款是同一个每月动作的两面。

branches.en: Both verbs describe the same contract seen from opposite ends.
branches.cn: 两个动词描述的是同一份租约，只是站在两端看。

intro.en: Rent is a short English word whose family grows with endings rather than prefixes.
intro.cn: rent 是一个简短英语词，它的词族主要靠词尾而不是前缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin reddere supplies the idea of giving back, and its deeper root dare means to give.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 reddere 提供「交还」的意思，更深的词根 dare 表示「给予」。

items.example: Red- appears in reddere, to give back.
items.exampleCN: red- 出现在 reddere（交还）中。

items.example: Dare is the source of many Latin verbs of handing over.
items.exampleCN: dare 是许多表示「交出」的拉丁动词的来源。

items.example: Reddere joins red- and dare into one verb.
items.exampleCN: reddere 把 red- 与 dare 合成一个动词。

items.example: Reddita lies behind the French word for income.
items.exampleCN: reddita 是法语中「收入」一词的前身。

items.example: Rente passes into English as rent.
items.exampleCN: rente 进入英语后写作 rent。

items.example: Rent names the payment for a home or land.
items.exampleCN: rent 指为住房或土地支付的款项。

items.example: Rental adds -al to the same stem.
Renter adds -er to name the person.

definition_zh: 非常；很；（限定用法）正是那个；极端的
definition_en: to a high degree, and, before a noun, the actual or exact one
core_image: 温度计的红柱一路顶到最上面那格
scene: 面试官看完简历，抬头说了一句：这份作品集非常出色。 The interviewer said that the portfolio was very impressive.
sceneCN: 这里 very 是「非常」（第 1 个义项：表示程度很高）；句意为面试官说这份作品集非常出色。温度计顶格的那个画面就是这个副词给人的感觉。

derivatives.zh: 短语，义为「非常；十分」
古旧副词，义为「确实地；真正地」

senses.title: To a high degree
senses.definition: used to strengthen an adjective or another adverb
senses.definitionCN: 用来加强形容词或副词的程度
senses.example: The interviewer said the portfolio was very impressive.
senses.exampleCN: 面试官说这份作品集非常出色。
senses.why: The oldest job of the word is simply to push a quality higher.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的作用，就是把某种性质往上推高。

senses.title: In a high degree with verbs
senses.definition: used with some verbs and participles to mean greatly
senses.definitionCN: 与某些动词或分词连用，表示程度很高
senses.example: She was very pleased with the result.
senses.exampleCN: 她对结果非常满意。
senses.why: With a participle the same word shifts from modifying a quality to modifying an action.
senses.whyCN: 与分词连用时，同一个词从修饰性质转为修饰动作。

senses.title: The actual or exact one
senses.definition: used before a noun to single out the exact person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指出正是某个人或某个事物
senses.example: That is the very book I was looking for.
senses.exampleCN: 那正是我在找的那本书。
senses.why: Pointing at one exact item is a short step from pushing a quality to its limit.
senses.whyCN: 从把性质推向极限，到指出唯一确切的那一个，只是一小步。

senses.title: The extreme end of something
senses.definition: used with a noun to mean the extreme or utmost
senses.definitionCN: 与名词连用，表示极端或极致
senses.example: They searched to the very end of the cave.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一直搜到洞穴的最深处。
senses.why: If a quality is pushed to the top, the noun that carries it is at its extreme.
senses.whyCN: 性质既被推到顶端，承载它的名词也就处在极端处。

senses.title: Used to add force in speech
senses.definition: used in speech for emphasis, as in the very idea
senses.definitionCN: 用于口语中加强语气，如 the very idea
senses.example: The very idea of moving abroad frightened him.
senses.exampleCN: 一想到要搬到国外，他就害怕。
senses.why: Emphasis in speech takes the same intensifying force and turns it on an idea.
senses.whyCN: 口语里的强调，把这股加强的力量转而用在某个念头上。

intro.en: Very began as a French adjective meaning true, and turned into the intensifier we use today.
intro.cn: very 最初是法语中意为「真实的」的形容词，后来变成今天的程度副词。

items.en: Verus meant true, and verax named the one who tells the truth.
items.cn: verus 意为真实的，verax 指说真话的人。

items.en: French verai carried the sense of genuine into everyday speech.
items.cn: 法语 verai 把「真正的」这一含义带入日常口语。

items.en: English verray first meant true or real, as in a verray friend.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 verray 最初意为真实的，如 a verray friend（真正的朋友）。

items.en: Placed before an adjective, it began to mean in a true degree, hence greatly.
items.cn: 放在形容词前时，它开始表示「真正地…」，进而表示「非常」。

items.en: The old sense survives only in fixed phrases such as the very same.
items.cn: 旧义如今只保留在 the very same 这类固定短语中。

note.en: The first group holds the small family of forms, the second the intensifiers and their opposites.
note.cn: 第一组是同族的小词群，第二组是程度副词及其反义说法。

entries.definition: truly, in old use
to a great degree
to check that something is true
to change or differ
to the highest degree
fairly, to a moderate degree
precise, with nothing added
to a small degree

normalIntro.en: From a Latin word for true to a word that simply turns the volume up: very has kept only its force.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁语中表示「真实」的词，到只负责把音量调大的词：very 只留下了那股加强的力量。

normal.en: Very and verify share the Latin root verus, true.
normal.cn: very 与 verify 同出拉丁语 verus（真实的）。

normal.en: Before a noun it means exact: the very man.
normal.cn: 放在名词前表示确切：the very man（正是那个人）。

normal.en: Before an adjective it means greatly: very cold.
normal.cn: 放在形容词前表示程度高：very cold（很冷）。

normal.en: It does not modify verbs directly; say very much like, not very like.
normal.cn: 它不直接修饰动词；要说 very much like，而非 very like。

normal.en: Comparative forms verier and veriest survive only in old books.
normal.cn: 比较级 verier、最高级 veriest 只存在于旧书中。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer whose red line goes to the top mark.
abstract.cn: 想一支温度计的红线顶到最上面一格。

abstract.en: Feel a speaker leaning forward to press one word harder.
abstract.cn: 感受说话人身子前倾，把某一个词压得更重。

abstract.en: See a spotlight picking out one single chair on a stage.
abstract.cn: 想聚光灯在舞台上圈出唯一一把椅子。

examples.en: The soup is very hot, so let it cool for a minute.
examples.cn: 汤很烫，让它凉一分钟。

examples.en: This is the very place where the two roads meet.
examples.cn: 这里正是两条路交汇的地方。

examples.en: He was not very happy about the change of plan.
examples.cn: 他对计划的变更不太满意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外瑞」——外边那位瑞哥嗓门特别大，一说就是「非常」响。

root: 拉丁语 verus（真实的）→ 古法语 verai → 中世纪英语 verray（真正的）→ 现代英语 very（非常）

sensesIntro.en: One little word grows from true, through truly to a plain intensifier, and keeps a second life as exactly that one.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个小词从「真实」出发，经「真正地」变成纯粹的程度副词，又保留了「正是那一个」的第二重身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thermometer pushed to its top mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计被推到最高那一格。

branches.en: The degree branch: a portfolio called impressive.
branches.cn: 程度分支：被称作出色的作品集。

branches.en: The verb branch: very pleased with the result.
branches.cn: 动词分支：对结果非常满意。

branches.en: The pointing branch: the very book on the shelf.
branches.cn: 指认分支：架上正是那本书。

branches.en: The extreme branch: the very end of the cave.
branches.cn: 极端分支：洞穴的最深处。

branches.en: The emphasis branch: the very idea frightens him.
branches.cn: 强调分支：光是这个念头就让他害怕。

intro.en: There is no living prefix here; the old root ver- (true) survives mainly inside longer words.
intro.cn: 这个词没有可拆的活前缀，古词根 ver-（真实）主要存活在更长的词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin verus gave French verai and English very; the same root also built verify, verity, and verdict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verus 派生法语 verai 与英语 very，同一词根还构成 verify、verity、verdict。

items.example: Ver- hides inside very as the sense of the genuine.
items.exampleCN: ver- 藏在 very 里，是「真正」的含义。

items.example: Very first meant in a true way.
items.exampleCN: very 最初表示「以真实的方式」。

items.example: We verify the figures before printing.
items.exampleCN: 付印前我们会核实这些数字。

items.meaning: a true saying by a jury
items.example: The jury returned a verdict of not guilty.
The verity of the claim was never in doubt.
items.exampleCN: 这一说法的真实性从未被怀疑。

items.example: She enjoyed the trip very much.
They wore the very same coat.
items.exampleCN: 他们穿的是完全相同的外套。

items.example: The film was not very long.

definition_zh: 相当；颇；完全；十分；的确
definition_en: to a fairly large degree; completely or entirely; used to agree strongly with what has just been said
core_image: 一杯水被倒到杯口，刚好齐平而不溢出
scene: 看完演出，两人站在剧院门口争论这出戏到底好不好，谁也没有立刻走开。 The play was quite good, but the ending felt rushed.
sceneCN: 这里 quite 是「相当、颇」（第 1 个义项：达到较大的程度但未到极致）；句意为这出戏相当不错，只是结尾显得仓促。画面里可留意：剧院门口的灯箱、还没散去的人群。

derivatives.zh: 与 quite 同源的形容词，用于 call it quits，指两清、扯平
同源动词，指停止或离开
re- 加同源词，指回报或报复

senses.title: To a fairly large degree
senses.definition: to a degree that is large but not extreme
senses.definitionCN: 达到较大但并未到极点的程度
senses.example: The film was quite good, though not great.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影相当不错，虽然算不上出色。
senses.why: The oldest sense was completely or free of qualification, and English softened it into a strong but not absolute degree.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「完全、毫无保留」，英语把它弱化为一种强而不绝对的程度。

senses.title: Completely or entirely
senses.definition: entirely, with no reservation, especially in British speech
senses.definitionCN: 完全地、毫无保留地，尤见于英式口语
senses.example: I quite agree with you on that point.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一点上我完全同意你。
senses.why: The word began as a legal term for being clear of a debt or a claim, and being clear of any doubt produced the sense of entirely.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是法律用语，指债务或主张已经清结；既然任何疑问都清除了，就生出「完全」这一层意思。

senses.title: Used to agree strongly
senses.definition: used alone or with a short reply to show strong agreement
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用或作简短回答，表示强烈的同意
senses.example: 'It is cold tonight.' 'Quite.'
senses.exampleCN: 「今晚真冷。」「的确。」
senses.why: If something is quite so, it is entirely so; a bare quite therefore affirms the previous statement without adding anything.
senses.whyCN: 如果某事 quite 如此，就是完全如此；单独一个 quite 因此是在肯定前一句话，不再另加内容。

intro.en: Quite comes from the same Latin root as quiet and quit, through a French word meaning cleared or free; from free of doubt came the sense of completely.
intro.cn: quite 与 quiet、quit 同出一个拉丁词根，经一个意为「清结、自由」的法语词传来；从「无疑」生出了「完全」的意思。

items.en: Quies meant rest, and the related adjective described a person or thing at rest and free from obligation.
items.cn: quies 意为休息，相关形容词形容处于安歇、免于义务的人或物。

items.en: Quietus was used in law for being cleared of a debt or a claim, that is, free and settled.
items.cn: quietus 在法律中用于表示债务或主张已清结，也就是自由、了结。

items.en: Old French quite carried the legal sense of cleared and free, and also the sense of entirely.
items.cn: 古法语 quite 既带有「清结、自由」的法律义，也带有「完全」义。

items.en: Middle English quite meant completely or without reservation, often in phrases of agreement.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quite 意为完全、毫无保留，常用于表示同意的说法。

items.en: Modern English weakened the word in everyday use to a fairly large degree, while keeping the older strong sense in British speech.
items.cn: 现代英语在日常用法中把它弱化为「相当」，而在英式口语里保留了较强的旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same root's English forms; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of degree and agreement.
note.cn: 形近组收同词根的英语形式；近义组收表示程度与同意的副词。

entries.definition: Silent and calm.
To stop or leave.
Even in a debt or a dispute, as in call it quits.
entries.definitionCN: 债务或争执两清，如 call it quits。

entries.definition: A literary word for calmness.
To a moderate degree.
To a noticeable degree, often with a mild tone.
entries.definitionCN: 达到明显程度地，常带轻微语气。

entries.definition: In every way, entirely.
In precise agreement with something.

normalIntro.en: The word began as cleared and free, moved to entirely, and softened to fairly in everyday speech.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「清结、自由」开始，走到「完全」，又在日常口语里弱化为「相当」。

normal.en: Quite, quiet and quit all come from the Latin word for rest; only quite kept the legal sense of settled.
normal.cn: quite、quiet 与 quit 都出自拉丁语「休息」一词，只有 quite 保留了「了结」的法律义。

normal.en: Quite a few means a fairly large number, even though few alone suggests a small one.
normal.cn: quite a few 意为相当多，尽管 few 单独用时表示很少。

normal.en: Not quite is the polite way of saying almost, but not completely.
normal.cn: not quite 是「几乎但不完全」的客气说法。

normal.en: In British speech quite can mean entirely, while in American speech it more often means fairly.
normal.cn: 在英式口语里 quite 可指完全，在美式口语里更常指相当。

normal.en: A single quite in reply means you agree completely with the previous sentence.
normal.cn: 单独一个 quite 作回答，表示你完全同意上一句话。

abstract.en: A word that once meant free of every claim now measures how much of a claim is true.
abstract.cn: 一个曾表示「免除一切主张」的词，如今用来衡量一项主张有多少成真。

abstract.en: Quite is a word of proportion, and proportion is always judged by the ear rather than by the ruler.
abstract.cn: quite 是一个讲分寸的词，而分寸总是由耳朵来判断，而不是由尺子。

abstract.en: The strength of quite depends on the listener, which is why the same sentence can sound like praise or like faint damning.
abstract.cn: quite 的分量取决于听者，所以同一句话既能听起来像称赞，也能像淡淡的贬低。

examples.en: The room is quite small, but it is enough for one person.
examples.cn: 房间相当小，但一个人住够了。

examples.en: Are you quite sure you left the keys here?
examples.cn: 你十分确定把钥匙落在这里了吗？

examples.en: There were quite a few people waiting outside.
examples.cn: 外面等着的人相当多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快特」——比「快」还要特别一点，程度相当高，记住 quite 是相当、完全。

root: 拉丁语 quies（休息）→ quietus（清结、免除）→ 古法语 quite → 英语 quite；同族有 quiet、quit、quits、requite。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being clear and complete; the senses divide into a strong degree, full completeness and bare agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「清结而完整」；义项分为较强程度、完全的完整性，以及单独表示同意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass filled to the brim, level but not spilling.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯水倒到杯口，齐平而不外溢。

branches.en: a film that is better than expected
branches.cn: 比预想更好的电影

branches.en: a debt marked paid in full
branches.cn: 标着「全部付清」的债务

branches.en: a single word of agreement in a quiet room
branches.cn: 安静房间里一个表示同意的单词

branches.en: the same word measuring a degree and closing a discussion
branches.cn: 同一个词既衡量程度，也结束讨论

branches.en: the legal fullness softened into everyday emphasis
branches.cn: 法律的「完全」被软化成日常的强调

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing on the Latin root of rest, and its English relatives are few but old.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「休息」词根上的法语借词，它的英语亲属不多但很古老。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root quiet- also produced quiet and quit, though English split the meanings apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 quiet- 也产生了 quiet 与 quit，只是英语把词义拆开了。

definition_zh: 发生；出现；碰巧；偶然遇到
definition_en: to take place or occur, often without being planned
core_image: 天上突然掉下一滴雨，正好落在路人的鼻尖上
scene: 上美术课时窗外忽然乌云密布，一场大雨说来就来。 What will happen if we forget our umbrellas?
sceneCN: 这里 happen 是「发生」（第 1 个义项：事情出现）；句意是如果我们忘带雨伞会发生什么呢。

derivatives.zh: 由 happen 加 -ing 构成，义为「发生的事情；事件」
由同根词 hap 加 -ly 构成，义为「偶然地；或许」（旧式）

senses.title: To take place
senses.definition: to occur, especially without being planned or controlled
senses.definitionCN: 出现、发生，尤指非计划或非可控之事
senses.example: A funny thing happened on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 回家路上发生了一件趣事。
senses.why: The raindrop lands where it will; events fall uninvited, so the verb means simply to occur.
senses.whyCN: 雨滴想落哪就落哪，事情不请自来，动词义就是「发生」。

senses.title: To do or be by chance
senses.definition: to have the chance fact of doing or being something
senses.definitionCN: 出于偶然而做了某事或处于某状态
senses.example: I happened to see her at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我碰巧在车站见到她。
senses.why: Chance can land on you as easily as rain; meeting by luck wears the same word.
senses.whyCN: 偶然像雨一样落在人身上，偶遇也套用同一个词。

senses.title: To come to someone's lot
senses.definition: to be experienced by someone, as in what happened to you
senses.definitionCN: 降临到某人身上，被某人经历
senses.example: Look what happened to my old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 看看我的旧自行车遭遇了什么。
senses.why: Events drop onto people from above, so the person becomes the landing spot.
senses.whyCN: 事件从天而降，人便成了落点。

senses.title: To exist as an event worth noting
senses.definition: to produce an event or excitement, as in nothing ever happens here
senses.definitionCN: 产生值得注意的事件或热闹，如这里从无事发生
senses.example: Nothing ever happens in this quiet town.
senses.exampleCN: 这座安静的小镇从无新闻。
senses.why: Where no drops fall, the ground stays dull; events are measured by their falling.
senses.whyCN: 没有雨滴落下，地面便沉闷；事件以「是否落下」来衡量。

intro.en: Happen grows from an old northern word for luck itself.
intro.cn: happen 从一个古老的北方词「运气」生长而来。

items.en: Old Norse happ meant good luck or chance, the seed of the whole family.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 happ 意为好运、机缘，是整个词族的种子。

items.en: Old English borrowed gehap meaning fitness or convenience.
items.cn: 古英语借入 gehap，意为适宜、便利。

items.en: Middle English hap meant luck, both good and bad.
items.cn: 中古英语 hap 意为运气，好坏皆可。

items.en: The verb happen was formed from hap with the -en ending, first meaning to come by chance.
items.cn: 由 hap 加 -en 构成动词 happen，最初意为偶然降临。

items.en: Modern English generalized it to any occurrence and kept happy, perhaps, mishap in the family.
items.cn: 现代英语泛化其义为任何事件，同族的 happy、perhaps、mishap 保留至今。

note.en: Words near happen in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 happen 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: the state of being happy
entries.definitionCN: 幸福；与 happen 同出古词 hap

entries.definition: a small unlucky accident
entries.definitionCN: 小灾小祸，同族词含 mis-（坏）

entries.definition: a tool that makes blades or pencils sharp
entries.definitionCN: 削具；与 happen 拼写尾部相近，实为 sharp 家族词

entries.definition: to take place, more formal
to happen to someone, literary
entries.definitionCN: 降临于（书面语），与 happen 第 3 义近

entries.definition: to happen, especially planned events
entries.definitionCN: 举行；发生，多指有安排之事

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks for happen.
normalIntro.cn: 五条 happen 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: happen comes from hap, old word for luck
normal.cn: happen 源自古词 hap（运气），先记词根。

normal.en: what happened is the top question phrase
normal.cn: what happened（怎么了）是最常用的疑问句式。

normal.en: happen to do adds the luck flavor
normal.cn: happen to do（碰巧做）自带运气味。

normal.en: accidents happen comforts small mistakes
normal.cn: accidents happen（意外难免）常用来安慰。

normal.en: happy shares the same old root
normal.cn: happy 与 happen 同根，「好运」生出「幸福」。

abstract.en: a raindrop landing on a bare nose
abstract.cn: 雨滴不偏不倚落在鼻尖。

abstract.en: a coin tossed and landing on its edge
abstract.cn: 硬币抛出，落成立着的罕见一幕。

abstract.en: an unplanned knock at the door
abstract.cn: 一记未经安排的敲门声。

examples.en: Nothing exciting ever happens in our street.
examples.cn: 我们这条街从没出过什么新鲜事。

examples.en: She happened to sit next to her best friend.
examples.cn: 她碰巧坐在好友旁边。

examples.en: Tell me what happened after the bell rang.
examples.cn: 告诉我铃响之后发生了什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿，喷」——嘿，突然喷出一桩新闻，happen 就是突然发生。

root: 源自古诺斯语 happ（好运、机缘），经中古英语 hap 加动词后缀 -en 构成 happen；同族词包括 happy、perhaps、mishap，核心画面是「不请自来的运气之雨」。

sensesIntro.en: From bare occurrence the verb widens to chance meetings, things falling on people, and towns with no news.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单纯的发生扩展到碰巧、事件临身，以及无事小镇的「没有发生」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: luck falling where it wants
core.cn: 核心意象：运气想落哪就落哪

branches.en: the event itself lands
branches.cn: 事件本身落地

branches.en: luck brushes a passerby
branches.cn: 运气擦过路人

branches.en: the person as landing spot
branches.cn: 人成为落点

branches.en: the silence of no events
branches.cn: 无事发生的寂静

branches.en: chance brushing a shoulder
branches.cn: 运气擦过肩膀的一瞬

intro.en: Happen carries one tiny suffix; the items below show its family and near rivals.
intro.cn: happen 只带一个小词尾，下面列出其词族与近义对手。

latinIntro.en: Latin-root rivals for the event field.
latinIntro.cn: 事件义场中的拉丁语系对手。

items.exampleCN: hap 加 en 构成 happen。

items.example: The concert was a happy happening.
items.exampleCN: 那场音乐会是一桩快乐的盛事。

items.example: By hap we met at the gate.

items.exampleCN: 一点小意外让我们耽误了。

items.example: The sports day is a big event.

definition_zh: 弱的；虚弱的；疲软的；差的；淡的
definition_en: not strong in body, force, effect or quality, and likely to give way under pressure
core_image: 一截被水泡软的细绳，拎起来时中间那段明显垮下去
scene: 雨下了整夜，屋檐下那根旧麻绳吸饱了水，挂上水桶后立刻往下坠。 The old rope was weak after the rain and sagged under the bucket.
sceneCN: 这里 weak 是「弱的」（第 1 个义项：力量不足、容易垮掉）；句意为雨后旧绳变得不结实，挂上水桶就往下坠。那截被水泡软、中间垮下去的绳子就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 弱的；虚弱的；疲软的；差的；淡的

derivatives.zh: 虚弱；弱点；嗜好
使变弱；减弱
虚弱地；无力地
体弱的人；软弱的人
腿软的；缺乏决断的

senses.title: Not strong in the body
senses.definition: having little physical strength, often because of illness or hunger
senses.definitionCN: 体力不足，常因疾病或饥饿所致
senses.example: After the fever he felt weak for several days.
senses.exampleCN: 退烧之后他虚弱了好几天。
senses.why: This is the bodily core: the muscles cannot do what they are asked to do.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体层面的核心：肌肉做不动被要求做的事。

senses.title: Likely to break or give way
senses.definition: easy to break, bend or damage under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下容易断裂、弯曲或损坏
senses.example: The rope was weak and snapped when the bucket filled.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子不结实，水桶装满就断了。
senses.why: The same lack of strength is then read into objects rather than bodies.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「力量不足」被从身体移到物体上。

senses.title: Low in force or intensity
senses.definition: small in force, loudness or brightness
senses.definitionCN: 力量、音量或亮度很小
senses.example: He answered in a weak voice from the back of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他在房间后面用微弱的声音回答。
senses.why: A light or a sound that carries little force is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 散发不出多少力量的光或声音，也用同一个词形容。

senses.title: Not convincing or effective
senses.definition: not convincing, persuasive or effective in argument or action
senses.definitionCN: 在论证或行动中不足以让人信服或产生效果
senses.example: That is a weak argument and the committee will reject it.
senses.exampleCN: 那个论据很无力，委员会会驳回它。
senses.why: An argument that cannot stand up to a question is pictured as giving way under load.
senses.whyCN: 经不起追问的论据，被想象成在重压下退让。

senses.title: Poor in quality or ability
senses.definition: below the usual standard, especially in a subject or skill
senses.definitionCN: 低于一般水平，尤指某学科或技能
senses.example: I am weak in spelling, so I keep a list of hard words.
senses.exampleCN: 我拼写很差，所以留了一份难词表。
senses.why: Weakness in a skill is judged against a standard, not against a muscle.
senses.whyCN: 技能上的「弱」是相对标准而言，与肌肉无关。

senses.title: Diluted or lacking strength
senses.definition: containing too much water or too little of the active substance
senses.definitionCN: 水太多或有效成分太少
senses.example: This tea is too weak; let it stand a little longer.
senses.exampleCN: 这茶太淡了，再泡一会儿。
senses.why: A drink without enough substance is as weak as a body without strength.
senses.whyCN: 缺少实质的饮品，与缺少力量的躯体一样「弱」。

senses.title: Lacking firmness of will
senses.definition: not firm in will or judgement, and easily led
senses.definitionCN: 意志或判断不坚定，容易被带动
senses.example: They called him weak for agreeing so quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 他们说他这么快就答应，是太软弱了。
senses.why: Moral strength is imagined as a force too, so a person without it is weak.
senses.whyCN: 道德力量也被想象成一种力气，缺少它的人便「弱」。

intro.en: Weak comes from Old Norse veikr, a word for bending or giving way, which replaced an Old English cousin of the same meaning.
intro.cn: weak 来自古诺斯语 veikr，意为弯下、退让，它取代了同义的古英语亲族词。

items.en: The Germanic root meant to bend or to yield, and it stands behind words for pliancy as well as weakness.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根意为弯曲、让步，既支撑柔顺类词，也支撑软弱类词。

items.en: Veikr described anything that gives way under pressure and entered English during the Norse settlements.
items.cn: veikr 形容在压力下退让的事物，在诺斯人定居时期进入英语。

items.en: The loan drove out the native weak-related form and settled in spelling as weyk or weak.
items.cn: 这一借词排挤了本土形式，拼写定为 weyk 或 weak。

items.en: The adjective spread from bodies to ropes, voices, arguments and tea.
items.cn: 这个形容词从身体扩展到绳子、声音、论据和茶。

items.en: Weak tea and a weak point show how far the single image of giving way reaches.
items.cn: weak tea 与 weak point 显示了「退让」这一意象延伸得多远。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the shape of weak, the second gives the words that compete with it.
note.cn: 第一组与 weak 同根或形近，第二组是与之竞争的近义词。

entries.definition: The state of being weak, or a fondness one cannot resist.
To make or become weak.
In a weak manner.
Seven days, pronounced exactly the same.
Easily broken, often of thin or delicate things.
Very weak, especially through age or illness.
Weak in light, sound or feeling.
Without the ability to act or change things.

normalIntro.en: Weak always means a shortage of force, whether in a body, a rope, a voice, an argument or a cup of tea.
normalIntro.cn: weak 始终表示力量不足，无论是身体、绳子、声音、论据还是一杯茶。

normal.en: Weak is the adjective; weakness is the noun; weaken is the verb.
normal.cn: weak 是形容词，weakness 是名词，weaken 是动词。

normal.en: Do not confuse weak with week, the seven days.
normal.cn: 不要把它与表示七天的 weekly 混淆。

normal.en: A weak point is where something gives way first.
normal.cn: weak point 是最先垮下的地方。

normal.en: Weak tea has too much water in the cup.
normal.cn: weak tea 是杯里水太多了。

normal.en: Weak in maths means below the class standard.
normal.cn: weak in maths 指低于班级水平。

abstract.en: Picture a wet rope sagging in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想一根湿绳中间明显下坠。

abstract.en: Hear a voice that barely reaches the far wall.
abstract.cn: 听一个几乎传不到远墙的声音。

abstract.en: Feel a handshake with no grip in it.
abstract.cn: 感受一次使不上劲的握手。

examples.en: She was still weak after the operation and slept most of the day.
examples.cn: 手术之后她仍然很虚弱，一天大部分时间都在睡。

examples.en: The bridge is old and weak, so heavy trucks are banned.
examples.cn: 这座桥又旧又不结实，因此禁止重型卡车通行。

examples.en: He is weak in grammar but very good at speaking.
examples.cn: 他语法很差，但口语很好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威克」——威克先生感冒后腿发软，连端起茶杯的力气都只剩一点点。

root: 日耳曼语词根（弯曲、退让）→ 古诺斯语 veikr（易弯、易垮）→ 中古英语 weak；同源词有 weakness、weaken。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts at a body without strength, then lends that shortage to ropes, voices, arguments, skills, drinks and wills.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从缺力气的身体出发，再把这份欠缺借给绳子、声音、论据、技能、饮品与意志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet rope sagging under a bucket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根湿绳在水桶下垮下去。

branches.en: The body branch: weak after a fever.
branches.cn: 身体分支：退烧后虚弱。

branches.en: The object branch: a rope that snaps.
branches.cn: 物体分支：会断的绳子。

branches.en: The intensity branch: a faint voice and thin tea.
branches.cn: 强度分支：微弱的声音与淡茶。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a weak argument and weak spelling.
branches.cn: 评判分支：无力的论据与很差的拼写。

branches.en: The will branch: too quick to agree.
branches.cn: 意志分支：答应得太快。

intro.en: Weak is the bare adjective, and the family is built with the ordinary English suffixes -ness, -en, -ly and -ling.
intro.cn: weak 是光杆形容词，词族由普通英语后缀 -ness、-en、-ly、-ling 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this Norse word, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词借自古诺斯语，并无拉丁来源，故拉丁表留空。

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 weak point 里。

definition_zh: 鼓励；激励；助长；怂恿
definition_en: to give someone hope, courage, or reason to do something
core_image: 把手放在对方背上轻推：勇气被推着往前走
scene: 赛前更衣室里队长逐个拍过队友的肩。 The captain encouraged every player before the match.
sceneCN: 这里 encourage 是「鼓励」（第 1 个义项：给人勇气）；句意是赛前队长鼓励了每一名队员。图中可辨识物件：更衣室、队服、搭肩的手、点头的队员。

derivatives.zh: 鼓励；鼓舞
令人鼓舞的
使泄气；劝阻

senses.title: To give courage to someone
senses.definition: to make someone feel more confident and hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 使某人更有信心和希望。
senses.example: The captain encouraged every player before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 赛前队长鼓励了每一名队员。
senses.why: The word literally means to put courage into someone, so the core is injecting bravery.
senses.whyCN: 该词字面即「把勇气注入某人」，核心是灌输胆气。

senses.title: To support or promote something
senses.definition: to help an activity grow by backing it
senses.definitionCN: 以支持促成某项活动的发展。
senses.example: The city encourages cycling with new lanes.
senses.exampleCN: 城市以新车道鼓励骑行。
senses.why: Backing a person generalizes into backing an activity or trend.
senses.whyCN: 支持某人泛化为支持某项活动或趋势。

senses.title: To make something bad more likely
senses.definition: to make it easier for something, often bad, to happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某事更易发生，常指坏事。
senses.example: Long queues encourage ticket touting.
senses.exampleCN: 长队助长了黄牛倒票。
senses.why: The same push that lifts good actions can lift bad ones.
senses.whyCN: 同一股推力既能推动好事，也能助长坏事。

intro.en: Encourage is literally the putting of courage into a heart.
intro.cn: encourage 字面即「把勇气放进心里」。

items.en: Old French corage meant heart or inner spirit.
items.cn: 古法语 corage 意为心、内在精神。

items.en: French encourager meant to embolden, to put heart into.
items.cn: 法语 encourager 意为壮胆、鼓气。

items.en: The root goes to Latin cor, the heart, source of cordial too.
items.cn: 词根出自拉丁语 cor（心），cordial 亦出于此。

items.en: English borrowed encourage in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入 encourage。

items.en: Its negative twin discourage grew by swapping the prefix.
items.cn: 其否定孪生词 discourage 通过替换前缀产生。

note.en: Two groups: same-prefix verbs and the courage field.
note.cn: 两组：同前缀动词与「勇气」语义场。

entries.definition: ordered or required formally
entries.definitionCN: 被责令的——开头相近，词义无关

entries.definition: to take courage away

definition_zh: 血；血液；血统；新鲜血液（新成员）
definition_en: the red liquid that flows through the body, family origin, or new members who bring fresh energy
core_image: 指尖划破后渗出的一滴红色液体
scene: 孩子摔倒擦破了膝盖，一滴血渗了出来。 A drop of blood came from the cut on his knee.
sceneCN: 这里 blood 是「血」（第 1 个义项：在体内流动的红色液体）；句意为他的膝盖伤口渗出一滴血。

pos.zh: 名词：血；血液；血统；新成员

senses.title: The red liquid
senses.definition: the red liquid that carries oxygen and food around the body
senses.definitionCN: 在体内运送氧气和养分的红色液体
senses.example: A drop of blood fell on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴血落在地板上。
senses.why: Old English blod named the red liquid itself, and this physical sense is still the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 blod 指的就是这种红色液体，这个身体层面的义项仍是词义的中心。

senses.title: Family origin
senses.definition: the family or national group a person comes from
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所属的家庭或民族群体
senses.example: She is of Italian blood.
senses.exampleCN: 她有意大利血统。
senses.why: Parents pass life to children through blood in old beliefs, so blood came to mean family origin.
senses.whyCN: 旧时认为父母通过血把生命传给孩子，于是 blood 引申为家族出身。

senses.title: New members
senses.definition: new people brought into a group to give it fresh energy
senses.definitionCN: 被引入某个群体、为其带来新活力的人
senses.example: The team needs new blood.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队需要新鲜血液。
senses.why: Fresh blood keeps a body alive, so new members are pictured as the blood a group needs.
senses.whyCN: 新鲜的血液让身体保持活力，所以新成员被比作一个群体所需要的血。

intro.en: Blood is an old English word with a Germanic family, and its figurative senses grew from the body to family and groups.
intro.cn: blood 是古老的英语词，属于日耳曼语族，它的比喻义从身体延伸到家族与群体。

items.en: Old English blod named the red liquid in the body and had the same shape as its Germanic relatives.
items.cn: 古英语 blod 指体内的红色液体，其词形与日耳曼语族诸词一致。

items.en: German Blut and Dutch bloed are close relatives, all pointing to one old word.
items.cn: 德语 Blut 与荷兰语 bloed 是近亲，都指向同一个古词。

items.en: Because life was thought to pass through blood, the word also came to mean family origin.
items.cn: 由于旧时认为生命通过血传递，这个词也用来表示家族出身。

items.en: Writers used blood for temper, courage and sacrifice, widening the word far beyond the body.
items.cn: 作家用 blood 指性情、勇气与牺牲，把这个词远远扩展到身体之外。

items.en: Today blood also means new members, as in new blood for a team.
items.cn: 今天 blood 还指新成员，如团队里的 fresh blood。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects words about life fluid and family.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收与体液、家族有关的词。

abstract.en: Follow the drop back through a family line and the word turns into origin.
abstract.cn: 让这一滴血沿着家族血脉回溯，这个词就变成了「出身」。

root: blood 来自古英语 blod，属于日耳曼语族，德语 Blut 与荷兰语 bloed 是同源词。它最初指体内流动的红色液体；由于旧时认为生命通过血传递，又引申为家族出身。后来作家用它指性情、勇气与牺牲，现代英语里还用它比喻团队中的新成员，即 new blood。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of blood rest on one picture: the red liquid of life, and then the family line and the fresh energy it stands for.
sensesIntro.cn: blood 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：生命所系的红色液体，以及它所代表的家族血脉与新鲜活力。

core.cn: 核心意象：擦破的膝盖上渗出的一滴血

branches.cn: 身体线：这种红色液体本身是最古老也最清楚的义项。

branches.cn: 血脉线：blood 承载着家族与民族出身的概念。

definition_zh: 决定；下决心；裁决；决定（结果）
definition_en: to choose what to do after thinking about it
core_image: 在心里把天平拨向一边的那只手
scene: 放学后大家讨论去哪里打球，最终有了主意。 We finally decide to play basketball in the park near school.
sceneCN: 这里 decide 是「决定」（第 1 个义项：思考后选定做法）；句意是我们最终决定在学校附近的公园打篮球。

collocations.phrase: make up your mind and decide

derivatives.zh: 由 decide 变词尾加 -sion 构成，义为「决定」
由 decide 的过去分词转成形容词，义为「明确的；坚决的」
由 decide 词根加 -ive 构成，义为「果断的；决定性的」
由 in-（不）加 decisive 构成，义为「犹豫不决的」

senses.title: To choose after thinking
senses.definition: to choose one thing to do after thinking about the choices
senses.definitionCN: 思考各种选择后选定要做的事
senses.example: I decide to join the reading club this term.
senses.exampleCN: 这学期我决定加入读书社。
senses.why: The mind weighs choices like a scale, then tips to one side.
senses.whyCN: 心里像天平一样称量各个选项，最后拨向一边，选定即决定。

senses.title: To settle a question officially
senses.definition: to settle a question or contest by an official judgement
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式判断解决争议或比赛结果
senses.example: The referee decides who wins the race.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判决定谁赢得赛跑。
senses.why: When two sides disagree, a judge's mind tips the scale for everyone.
senses.whyCN: 双方争执不下时，由裁判心中的天平替所有人拨向一边，于是有了裁决义。

senses.title: To strongly affect a result
senses.definition: to strongly control what the result will be
senses.definitionCN: 强烈左右结果
senses.example: One goal decided the whole match.
senses.exampleCN: 一个进球决定了整场比赛。
senses.why: The hand that tips the scale controls the outcome, so key moments were said to decide.
senses.whyCN: 拨动天平的手掌控结果，于是关键时刻被称为决定性时刻，这是从意象自然延伸的用法。

intro.en: Decide comes from a Latin word for cutting off other choices.
intro.cn: decide 来自拉丁语中表示「切断其他选项」的词。

items.en: Decidere meant to cut off, formed from de- (off) plus caedere (to cut).
items.cn: 拉丁语 decidere 意为切断，由 de-（离开）加 caedere（切）构成。

items.en: In Roman courts decidere meant to settle a dispute by cutting away doubt.
items.cn: 在罗马法庭上 decidere 表示斩除疑虑、裁定争议。

items.en: Old French carried decider into learned writing.
items.cn: 古法语把 decider 带进书面语。

items.en: English took decide in the fourteenth century, first in law and argument.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 decide，最初用于法律和论辩。

items.en: Daily life widened it to every small choice, from lunch to teams.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到日常大小选择，从午饭到组队都用。

note.en: These words share the Latin root caedere or describe making choices.
note.cn: 这些词与拉丁词根 caedere 同源，或同样描述做选择。

abstract.en: Picture scissors snipping away every path but one.
abstract.cn: 想象剪刀把除了一条路之外的所有路都剪断。

abstract.en: Hear a judge's gavel cut the noise in half.
abstract.cn: 听法槌一响，把嘈杂声一切两半。

abstract.en: Feel the scale tip in your mind with a click.
abstract.cn: 体会心中天平咔哒一声拨向一边。

examples.en: We decide to give our old toys to the children in the village.
examples.cn: 我们决定把旧玩具送给村里的孩子们。

examples.en: The captain decides when the team should rest.
examples.cn: 队长决定球队何时休息。

examples.en: One piece of bread decided the picnic: it was the last food left.
examples.cn: 最后一块面包成了野餐的关键：那是仅剩的食物。

definition_zh: 监狱；监禁；羁押场所；牢笼
definition_en: a building where convicted people are kept as punishment; the state of being kept there; a place of legal custody; and, figuratively, any situation a person cannot escape
core_image: 一扇高窗把光切成窄条，落在铁栏后面的石地上
scene: 雨夜里，高墙顶端只亮着一盏灯，铁门在身后合上，声音沉得像石头落进水里。 He spent many years in a prison built on the edge of the moor.
sceneCN: 这里 prison 指「监狱」（第 1 个义项：关押已判刑者的建筑）；句意为他在荒原边上的一座监狱里度过了许多年。图中可辨识物件：高墙、灯、合上的铁门。

pos.zh: 监狱；监禁；羁押场所；牢笼

derivatives.zh: 由 prison 加表人后缀 -er 构成，义为「囚犯；俘虏」
由 prison 加表示「使进入」的前缀 im- 构成，义为「监禁；关押」
由 imprison 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「监禁；关押」

senses.title: A building where convicted people are kept
senses.definition: a building, usually with cells and high walls, where people are kept as punishment for crimes
senses.definitionCN: 通常设有牢房和高墙、用来关押罪犯以示惩罚的建筑
senses.example: The old prison is now a museum of penal history.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧监狱如今是刑罚史博物馆。
senses.why: The French noun named both the fact of captivity and the place of it, and the place is the sense that ordinary speech keeps at the front.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语名词既指被囚禁这件事，也指囚禁的地方；日常语言放在最前面的，是地方这一层。

senses.title: The state of being kept in such a place
senses.definition: the condition of being locked away as a legal punishment, used especially after the preposition in and without an article
senses.definitionCN: 作为法律惩罚被关起来的状态，尤用于介词 in 之后且不带冠词
senses.example: She has been in prison for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 她已入狱三年。
senses.why: Because the same noun could name captivity itself, English can use it as a mass noun after in, where no article is needed and no particular building is meant.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词本身就能指被囚禁的状态，英语便可以让它在 in 之后当不可数名词用，既不需要冠词，也不指某一座具体的建筑。

senses.title: A place of legal custody for people awaiting trial
senses.definition: a place where the law holds people who have not yet been tried or sentenced
senses.definitionCN: 法律上关押尚未受审或尚未判刑者的地方
senses.example: In older records, the town prison held debtors and people awaiting trial.
senses.exampleCN: 在更早的记载里，镇上的羁押所关过欠债的人和候审的人。
senses.why: Legal Latin and French used one word for anyone held by the law, whether sentenced or waiting, and older records keep that wider use although modern systems split the buildings.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语和法语用同一个词指任何被法律看管的人，无论已判未判；旧记载保留了这个更宽的用法，尽管现代制度把两类建筑分开了。

senses.title: A place or situation from which one cannot escape
senses.definition: any place, relationship or habit that traps a person the way a cell traps a prisoner
senses.definitionCN: 像牢房困住囚犯那样，把人困住的任何地方、关系或习惯
senses.example: His own fame had become a prison he could not leave.
senses.exampleCN: 他自己的名气成了一座他走不出去的牢笼。
senses.why: A walled place is easy to move onto anything that keeps a person in, so the word follows the feeling of being enclosed rather than the stone.
senses.whyCN: 一座有围墙的地方很容易被挪去指任何把人困住的东西，所以这个词跟着的是被围住的感觉，而不是石头。

intro.en: Prison comes from a Latin verb for seizing: the word first names the act of taking a person, then the holding, then the building where the holding happens.
intro.cn: prison 出自拉丁语中表示「抓」的动词：这个词先指把人拿住这个动作，再指看管，最后指看管发生的那座建筑。

items.en: The Latin verb prehendere meant to seize or take hold of, formed from the prefix pre- and a root for grasping.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 prehendere 意为抓住、拿住，由前缀 pre- 加一个表示抓握的词根构成。

items.en: Its noun prehensio named the act of seizing, and by extension the holding of a person in custody.
items.cn: 它的名词 prehensio 指拿获这个动作，引申为把人看管起来。

items.en: Spoken Latin shortened the form to prensio, and it is this shorter stem that passed into French.
items.cn: 口语拉丁语把词形缩成 prensio，进入法语的正是这个较短的词干。

items.en: Old French prison meant both captivity and the place of captivity, and English borrowed it after the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 古法语 prison 既指被囚禁，也指囚禁的地方；诺曼征服之后英语借入这个词。

items.en: Middle English prisoun settled into modern prison, keeping the building and the state, and later took on the figurative sense of any trap.
items.cn: 中古英语 prisoun 定型为现代 prison，同时保留建筑与状态两义，后来又添上「任何牢笼」的比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin seizing stem and the English words built on prison; the near-meaning group gathers the other names for places and states of confinement.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语表示抓取的词干与由 prison 构成的英语词展开；近义组收其他表示关押地点与关押状态的词。

entries.definition: To put someone in prison; formed with the prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人关进监狱；由前缀 im- 构成。

entries.definition: The act or state of being kept in prison.
A person kept in prison or held captive.
entries.definitionCN: 被关在监狱里或被俘获的人。

entries.definition: Able to grasp, as a monkey's tail does; built on the same Latin root for seizing.
entries.definitionCN: 能够抓握的，如猴子的尾巴；建立在同一个表示抓取的拉丁词根上。

entries.definition: A place for people held for short periods or awaiting trial; the lighter everyday word in many varieties.
entries.definitionCN: 关押短期服刑者或候审者的地方；在许多英语变体里是较轻的日常说法。

entries.definition: A small room in a prison in which one prisoner is kept.
entries.definitionCN: 监狱里关押一名囚犯的小房间。

entries.definition: The state of being kept inside a closed space.
entries.definitionCN: 被关在封闭空间里的状态。

entries.definition: A prison, especially in American English, for people serving long sentences.
entries.definitionCN: 尤用于美式英语，指关押长期服刑者的监狱。

normalIntro.en: Everything in this family goes back to a Latin verb for grabbing a person, so the reminders follow the movement from seizing to holding to the walls that keep the holding in place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族的一切都回到拉丁语中「抓住一个人」的动词，所以记忆线索跟着从拿获、看管到砌起围墙这条路线走。

normal.en: Prehendere is Latin for seize, so a prison is where the people who have been seized are kept.
normal.cn: prehendere 是拉丁语的「抓住」，所以 prison 就是关住那些被抓住之人的地方。

normal.en: Old French used one word for both the place and the state, which is why English says in prison without an article.
normal.cn: 古法语用同一个词指地方和状态，所以英语说 in prison 时不加冠词。

normal.en: Imprison adds the prefix im-, the same in- that appears in enclose: to put someone inside.
normal.cn: imprison 加了前缀 im-，就是 enclose 里的那个 in-，意思是把人放进去。

normal.en: Prisoner adds -er, the old French ending for a person concerned with something.
normal.cn: prisoner 加了 -er，那是古法语里表示「与某事相关的人」的词尾。

normal.en: Jail and prison are near twins, but prison is the heavier word and usually names the place for long sentences.
normal.cn: jail 与 prison 像一对双胞胎，但 prison 分量更重，通常指关长期刑期的地方。

abstract.en: The word travels from a hand closing on an arm to a wall closing on a life.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一只抓住胳膊的手，走到一堵围住一生的墙。

abstract.en: Prison as a state needs no article, because captivity is treated as a condition rather than as a building.
abstract.cn: 作为状态的 prison 不带冠词，因为被囚禁被当成一种处境，而不是一座建筑。

abstract.en: Once a noun names a walled place, it can be moved onto any boundary that holds a person in.
abstract.cn: 一旦一个名词指过有围墙的地方，它就能被挪去指任何把人困住的界线。

examples.en: The old prison is now a museum of penal history.
examples.cn: 那座旧监狱如今是刑罚史博物馆。

examples.en: She has been in prison for three years.
examples.cn: 她已入狱三年。

examples.en: His own fame had become a prison he could not leave.
examples.cn: 他自己的名气成了一座他走不出去的牢笼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普里森」——人被关进石头墙里，只能听见自己的呼吸声。

root: 古法语 prison（囚禁、监牢）经中古英语 prisoun 进入现代英语；更早可上溯到拉丁语 prehensio（拿获），动词 prehendere（抓住）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person being seized and held; the senses divide into the building, the condition, the legal custody that precedes sentencing, and the figurative trap.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一个人被抓并被看住」；义项由此分出建筑、状态、判刑前的法律羁押，以及比喻的牢笼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: narrow strips of light falling through a high window onto a stone floor behind bars.
core.cn: 核心意象：高窗把光切成窄条，落在铁栏后的石地上。

branches.en: a high window cutting light into strips
branches.cn: 高窗把光切成窄条

branches.en: a visiting hour counted in minutes
branches.cn: 以分钟计的探视时间

branches.en: a cell door closing before a trial
branches.cn: 审判前关上的牢门

branches.en: a town where everyone knows your name
branches.cn: 人人都知道你名字的小镇

branches.en: the same walls holding both the sentenced and the waiting
branches.cn: 同一堵墙关着已判的人和候审的人

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of seizing, its noun of arrest, the French noun of captivity, the English borrowing, and the endings that build prisoner and imprisonment from it.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示抓取的拉丁语动词、表示逮捕的名词、法语中表示囚禁的名词、英语借词，以及由此构成 prisoner 与 imprisonment 的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Prehendere and its noun prehensio are securely recorded in Latin, and the shortened prensio explains the French form that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: prehendere 及其名词 prehensio 在拉丁语里有明确记录，缩短的 prensio 则解释了英语所借的那个法语词形。

definition_zh: 污染；污染状态；有害物质或能量进入环境并造成损害
definition_en: the introduction of harmful substances or energy into the environment, or the state of being damaged by them
core_image: 河湾水面浮着一层彩色油光，岸边芦苇被塑料绳缠住，清水已成危险之物
scene: 河湾的水面漂着一层彩色油光，岸边芦苇被塑料绳缠住。 Pollution had turned the once clear river into a hazard.
sceneCN: 这里 pollution 指「水体受到有害物质侵入而变坏的状态」（第 4 个义项：水污染使水体失去原有用途）；句意为污染把曾经清澈的河变成了危险之地。图中可辨识物件：河湾、油光水膜、塑料绳、芦苇；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 污染；污染状态（不可数为主，复数指多种或多次污染）

derivatives.zh: 污染；弄脏
污染物
污染者
受污染的

senses.title: Harmful matter or energy entering the environment
senses.titleCN: 有害物质或能量进入环境
senses.definition: the act of putting harmful substances or excess energy into air, water or soil
senses.definitionCN: 把有害物质或过量能量放入空气、水体或土壤的行为
senses.example: Pollution had turned the once clear river into a hazard.
senses.exampleCN: 污染把曾经清澈的河变成了危险之地。
senses.why: The word names the act before it names the result: something is put into a medium that was not there before.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先命名动作，再命名结果：某物被放进了本来没有它的介质里。

senses.title: The damaged state of a medium
senses.definition: the condition of air, water or land after harmful matter has entered it
senses.definitionCN: 空气、水或土地在有害物质进入之后所处的状态
senses.example: The lake's pollution was visible as a green scum.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水的污染表现为一层绿色浮沫。
senses.why: English uses the same noun for the act and its result, so pollution can be what was done and what is now there.
senses.whyCN: 英语用同一个名词兼指动作与结果，因此 pollution 既可以是「做了什么」，也可以是「现在有什么」。

senses.title: Air pollution
senses.definition: the presence of smoke, gases or particles in the air at harmful concentrations
senses.definitionCN: 烟、气体或颗粒以有害浓度存在于空气中
senses.example: Winter air pollution settles over the plain and hides the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季的空气污染压在平原上，把群山遮住。
senses.why: Coal smoke made this sense the first and most visible kind of pollution in industrial cities.
senses.whyCN: 煤烟使这个义项成为工业城市里最早、最可见的一种污染。

senses.title: Water pollution
senses.definition: the entry of sewage, chemicals or waste into rivers, lakes, groundwater or the sea
senses.definitionCN: 污水、化学品或废物进入河流、湖泊、地下水或海洋
senses.example: Water pollution from the tannery reached the wells downstream.
senses.exampleCN: 制革厂造成的水污染波及下游的水井。
senses.why: Water carries harm away from the source, so the word stresses the medium that spreads it.
senses.whyCN: 水把危害从源头带走，这个词于是强调传播它的介质。

senses.title: Soil and land pollution
senses.definition: the accumulation of harmful substances in soil, or the degradation of land by waste
senses.definitionCN: 有害物质在土壤中累积，或土地因废物而退化
senses.example: Soil pollution kept the allotments out of use for years.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤污染让这些菜地多年不能使用。
senses.why: Soil holds what air and water deliver, so pollution here is a deposit that stays in place.
senses.whyCN: 土壤承接空气与水送来的东西，这里的污染是留在原地的沉积。

senses.title: Noise, light and heat pollution
senses.definition: excess energy that harms health, wildlife or the quality of a place without adding substance
senses.definitionCN: 过量的能量，不添加物质却危害健康、野生生物或环境品质
senses.example: Light pollution erased the stars above the coastal towns.
senses.exampleCN: 光污染抹去了沿海城镇上空的星空。
senses.why: Modern regulation widened the word to energy, because harm does not require a material to be present.
senses.whyCN: 现代监管把这个词扩展到能量，因为造成危害并不需要有物质在场。

senses.title: Plastic and marine pollution
senses.definition: the accumulation of persistent waste, especially plastics, in oceans and on shores
senses.definitionCN: 持久性废物、尤其是塑料，在海洋与海岸上的累积
senses.example: Marine pollution washed ashore as bottle caps and netting.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋污染以瓶盖和网绳的形式冲上岸。
senses.why: A single material became so dominant that it earned its own use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 单一材料变得如此突出，以至于单独占用了这个词的一种用法。

senses.title: Ritual or moral defilement
senses.definition: the historical sense of making something sacred or pure unclean
senses.definitionCN: 使神圣或纯洁之物变得不洁的旧义
senses.example: The old texts speak of pollution that required a rite of cleansing.
senses.exampleCN: 古籍中说到需要行洁净礼才能解除的玷污。
senses.why: The word entered English as a religious term, and the environmental sense is a later branch of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以宗教术语进入英语，环境义是同一意象后来分出的枝。

senses.title: Abstract: degradation of information or discourse
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：信息与言论环境的变质
senses.definition: a transferred use for the flooding of a field with false, low-quality or manipulative content
senses.definitionCN: 转指某领域被虚假、低质或操纵性内容淹没
senses.example: Information pollution makes a reliable source harder to find.
senses.exampleCN: 信息污染使可靠来源更难找到。
senses.why: The metaphor preserves the structure: a shared medium is filled with something that lowers its value for everyone.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了结构：共用的介质被填入某物，使它对所有人都贬值。

intro.en: Pollution came to English through French from Latin pollutio, a noun of defilement. Its oldest English sense is religious; the environmental sense is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pollution 经法语来自拉丁 pollutio，是一个表示「玷污」的名词。它最早的英语义项是宗教性的，环境义则是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: The verb behind the noun is usually divided into por- (a form of pro- 'forth') and luere 'to wash'. The deeper origin of luere is uncertain, and the relation sometimes drawn to lavare 'to wash' is a related-form hypothesis, not a proved descent.
items.cn: 这个名词背后的动词通常拆成 por-（pro-「向前」的一种形式）与 luere「洗」。luere 的更深来源不确定，有人把它与 lavare「洗」联系，那只是「相关形式」的假说，并非已证实的承继。

items.en: Polluere meant 'to defile, to corrupt'. How the washing element came to mean defiling is not fully explained; one account treats the prefix as intensive rather than directional.
items.cn: polluere 意为「弄脏、败坏」。「洗」的成分如何转为「弄脏」，并未得到完整解释；一种说法把前缀视为加强成分而非方向成分。

items.en: Late Latin pollutio named a defiling, especially ritual uncleanness, and this is the sense that entered English.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 pollutio 指玷污，尤指仪式上的不洁，进入英语的正是这一义项。

items.en: From the fourteenth century English pollution meant the desecration of sacred things or the state of being ritually unclean.
items.cn: 从十四世纪起，英语 pollution 指对神圣之物的亵渎或仪式上的不洁状态。

items.en: In the nineteenth century smoke, sewage and factory waste gave the word its modern environmental sense, and it soon became a public-health issue.
items.cn: 十九世纪，烟、污水与工厂废料赋予这个词现代环境义，它很快成为公共卫生议题。

items.en: Source uncertain (internal history of polluere, first date of the environmental sense): the semantic path from washing to defiling is unexplained and the first environmental citation is not fixed, so its date is approximate; any older form offered for luere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（polluere 的内部构造、环境义的首见年代）：从「洗」到「弄脏」的语义路径未获解释，环境义的最早书证也无定论，年代只能约计；凡为 luere 给出的更早形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same pollute stock that differ in grammar or role; group two holds other words for environmental damage, each naming a different part of the problem.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 pollute 词干、语法角色不同的形式；第二组是其他表示环境损害的词，各自命名问题的一个不同部分。

entries.definition: A single offending substance; pollution is the resulting condition or the whole accumulation.
entries.definitionCN: 一种肇事的物质；pollution 是造成的结果或整体累积。

entries.definition: To put harmful matter into a medium; the noun names what the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 把有害物质放入介质；名词指动词所产生的状态。

entries.definition: A person or firm that pollutes; it is a responsible party, not a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 造成污染的人或企业；它是责任方，而非状态。

entries.definition: A head, a vote survey or a hornless beast, from Middle English polle; the resemblance to pollute is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指头、投票调查或无角牲畜，出自中古英语 polle；与 pollute 的相似只是偶然。

entries.definition: The making impure of a substance or product; it need not harm an ecosystem, which pollution implies.
entries.definitionCN: 使物质或产品不纯；它未必危害生态，而 pollution 含有这一层。

entries.definition: A general lowering of quality or condition; pollution is one cause of environmental degradation.
entries.definitionCN: 品质或状况的普遍下降；污染是环境退化的一个原因。

entries.definition: The release of a substance into the air; pollution is the harm that follows from such releases.
entries.definitionCN: 物质向空气的排放；pollution 是这类排放带来的危害。

entries.definition: The clogging or dirtying of equipment, hulls or beds; it is a practical nuisance sense, not a public-health one.
entries.definitionCN: 设备、船体或床层的堵塞与污损；它是设备层面的麻烦义，而非公共卫生义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pollution is the noun of pollute: the act of putting harm into a medium and the state that follows.
normal.cn: pollution 是 pollute 的名词：把危害放入介质的动作，以及随之而来的状态。

normal.en: The family runs pollute, pollutant, polluter, polluted and polluting.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pollute、pollutant、polluter、polluted 与 polluting。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the medium: air pollution, water pollution, soil pollution, noise pollution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出介质：空气污染、水污染、土壤污染、噪声污染。

normal.en: The oldest English sense was religious: pollution meant ritual uncleanness before it meant smoke.
normal.cn: 最早的英语义项是宗教性的：pollution 先指仪式上的不洁，后指烟尘。

normal.en: Poll looks alike but means 'head', so it is a false relative.
normal.cn: poll 形似而同源无关，意为「头」，是假同源。

abstract.en: Picture a clear river receiving one pipe and losing its colour downstream.
abstract.cn: 想象一条清河接入一根管子，下游就失了颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a night sky erased by a ring of lamps.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈路灯抹掉了夜空。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf filled with books that repeat nonsense.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上塞满反复讲胡话的书。

examples.en: Pollution in the estuary comes from farms far upstream.
examples.cn: 河口处的污染来自远在上游的农田。

examples.en: The city monitors pollution every hour at ten stations.
examples.cn: 该市在十个监测站每小时监测污染。

examples.en: Noise pollution from the highway reaches the school.
examples.cn: 公路的噪声污染传到了学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pollute（污染）+ ion」——把脏东西放进环境这件事，以及它造成的状态 → 污染

root: 拉丁 pollutio「玷污」< polluere「弄脏」；polluere 通常拆为 por-（pro- 变体）+ luere「洗」，但「洗」转为「弄脏」未获完整解释，luere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one intrusion: a clean medium is entered, its state changes, each medium gets its own name, energy and waste join the list, and the old religious image survives at one end while the metaphor of a spoiled shared medium survives at the other.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一次侵入展开：洁净介质被进入，状态改变，各介质各得一名，能量与废物加入清单，一端留着旧的宗教意象，另一端留着「共用介质被弄坏」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an oily sheen on a river bend, with reeds tangled in plastic cord.
core.cn: 核心意象：河湾上一层油光，芦苇缠着塑料绳。

branches.en: ACT AND STATE: English uses one noun for the putting-in and for what is left afterwards.
branches.cn: 动作与状态：英语用同一个名词兼指「放入」与「放入后剩下的」。

branches.en: THREE MEDIA: air, water and soil each make pollution visible in a different way.
branches.cn: 三种介质：空气、水与土壤各以不同方式让污染显形。

branches.en: ADDED ENERGY AND WASTE: noise, light and plastic all fit the same frame of something extra.
branches.cn: 能量与废物：噪声、光与塑料都落在「多出来的东西」这同一框架里。

branches.en: OLD ROOT: ritual defilement is the image from which the environmental sense grew.
branches.cn: 旧根：仪式上的玷污是环境义从中长出的意象。

branches.en: NEW ROOT: information pollution repeats the image in a shared medium of thought.
branches.cn: 新枝：信息污染在同一意象上重复，只是介质成了共用的思想空间。

intro.en: Pollution is a Latin noun of action with a debated root, so the suffix and prefix are clear while the semantic history of the root is not.
intro.cn: pollution 是拉丁动作名词，词根有争议，因此前缀与后缀清楚，而词根的语义历史不清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin polluere gives pollute, pollution, pollutant and polluter; -io, -ionis forms nouns of action in English -ion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 polluere 衍生 pollute、pollution、pollutant 与 polluter；-io, -ionis 在英语中构成 -ion 动作名词。

items.example: One account reads the prefix as directional.
items.exampleCN: 一种说法把这个前缀读作方向性的。

items.example: The washing element is the disputed half of the verb.

definition_zh: 数学；数学课；数学运算
definition_en: the science of numbers, quantities, and shapes, or the school subject that teaches it; informal American English for mathematics
core_image: 黑板上写满数字与公式，一支粉笔正在解题
scene: 铃声响起，同学们收起练习册走向下一间教室。 She got the highest score in the class on the math test.
sceneCN: 这里指学校科目「数学」（第 1 个义项：作为学科或科学的数学）；句意为她在全班数学测验中得了最高分。

pos.zh: 数学；数学课（美式口语，为 mathematics 的缩略）

derivatives.zh: math 的完整正式形式，义为「数学」这门学科
由 mathematics 加后缀 -al 构成，义为「数学的；精确的」

senses.title: The school subject or science of numbers
senses.definition: the study or science of numbers, quantities, shapes, and the relationships between them
senses.definitionCN: 研究数、量、形及其关系的学问，也指学校里教这门知识的课程
senses.example: Math is her favorite subject at school.
senses.exampleCN: 数学是她在学校最喜欢的科目。
senses.why: The word is simply a clipped, informal form of mathematics, so it keeps the full academic meaning in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: math 只是 mathematics 的口语缩略形式，所以完整保留了「数学」这门学科的学术含义，只是在日常口语中更简短随意。

senses.title: A calculation or the act of computing
senses.definition: a calculation or piece of arithmetic, especially in the informal phrase do the math
senses.definitionCN: 指一次计算或算术运算，尤其在口语短语 do the math（算一算）中
senses.example: Do the math: three tickets at ten dollars each is thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 算一算：三张票每张十美元，一共三十美元。
senses.why: Because the subject is about calculating, English naturally extends the word to the act of calculating itself.
senses.whyCN: 由于这门学科的本质就是计算，英语顺势把 math 从「学科」引申为「算一算」这个动作本身，带有让人自己想明白的口吻。

intro.en: Math is a modern English clipping of mathematics, which traces back through Latin and Greek to a root about learning and thinking.
intro.cn: math 是现代英语对 mathematics 的口语截短，后者经拉丁语源自希腊语，本义与「学习、思考」相关。

items.en: The Greek noun mathema meant 'that which is learned', from the verb manthanein 'to learn'; the derived adjective mathematikos referred to what pertains to learning, later especially to mathematical study.
items.cn: 希腊语名词 mathema 意为「所学之物」，来自动词 manthanein（学习）；派生形容词 mathematikos 指与学习有关的，后来专指数学研究。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as mathematicus, and mathematica (a plural noun) named the mathematical sciences, preserving the Greek sense of 'the things worth learning'.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊语形容词作 mathematicus，复数名词 mathematica 用来命名「数学诸学科」，保留了「值得学习的学问」这层希腊语义。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as mathematique, part of the learned vocabulary carried through medieval universities.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语作 mathematique，是中世纪大学学术词汇的一部分。

items.en: Middle English took mathematics from Old French and Latin in the fourteenth century, at first covering all learned sciences before narrowing to the science of numbers.
items.cn: 中古英语在十四世纪经古法语和拉丁语借入 mathematics，最初泛指各门学问，后来才收窄为「数与形的科学」。

items.en: In nineteenth-century American English, mathematics was clipped to maths-style informal forms: Americans favored math while British English favored maths; the clipped form then spread worldwide through American schooling and media.
items.cn: 十九世纪美国英语把 mathematics 截短：美国人偏好 math，英式英语偏好 maths；这一缩略形式随美国教育和传媒传遍世界。

note.cn: 与 math 拼写或发音相近的词，以及意义相近的词。

normalIntro.en: Straightforward memory hooks built from the word's real history and use.

normal.cn: math 就是 mathematics 剪掉尾巴，就像 photo 之于 photograph，学科教名变口语短词。

normal.en: British maths keeps the s, American math drops it: same subject, two flags.
normal.cn: 英式 maths 带 s，美式 math 不带：同一门学科，两种旗号。

normal.en: In the phrase 'do the math', math means the calculating itself.
normal.cn: 在短语 do the math（算一算）里，math 指计算动作本身，让人自己想明白。

normal.en: The Greek root manthanein means 'to learn', so mathematics is literally 'the learning'.
normal.cn: 希腊词根 manthanein 意为「学习」，所以 mathematics 字面上就是「所学之学」。

normal.en: math problem, math test, math class: it always names the school subject first.
normal.cn: math problem、math test、math class：它首先用来命名学校里的数学课与数学题。

abstract.en: Picture a chalkboard crowded with digits, and one letter of 'mathematics' being erased at a time until only 'math' remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一块写满数字的黑板，mathematics 的字母被一个个擦掉，最后只剩 math，越擦越口语。

abstract.en: Hear the bell ring after a math test: the word is short because students want a short word for it.
abstract.cn: 听到数学测验结束的铃声：这个词这么短，正因为学生们想要一个短词来叫它。

abstract.en: See yourself saying 'do the math' with a raised eyebrow, letting numbers do the arguing for you.
abstract.cn: 想象你挑眉说一句「你自己算算」，让数字替你把道理讲完。

examples.en: If each ticket costs ten dollars, do the math before you invite five friends.
examples.cn: 如果每张票十美元，邀请五个朋友之前先自己算算账。

examples.en: He is good at math but struggles with writing essays.

definition_zh: 迅速地；立刻；敏捷地
definition_en: at high speed; after only a short time; with a fast mind or fast reaction
core_image: 秒针扫过表盘，几乎来不及看清刻度
scene: 厨房里水开了，她一手关火，一手把面条下进锅里，动作没有半点停顿。 She quickly moved the pot off the burner before the water boiled over.
sceneCN: 这里 quickly 是「迅速地、动作很快地」（第 1 个义项：以很高的速度做某事）；句意为她迅速把锅从炉子上移开，免得水溢出来。画面里可留意：关火的手、下锅的面条、腾起的白汽。
