senses.title: At high speed
senses.definition: at a high speed, so that little time is taken
senses.definitionCN: 以很高的速度，因此只花很少时间
senses.example: She finished the test quickly and checked her answers.
senses.exampleCN: 她很快做完试卷，又检查了一遍答案。
senses.why: The adverb simply adds the manner ending to the adjective of speed, so it describes how an action is carried out.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是在表示速度的形容词后加了方式词尾，因此描述动作是以什么方式进行的。

senses.title: After only a short time
senses.definition: within a short time after something else happens
senses.definitionCN: 在某事发生后很短的时间内
senses.example: The sky darkened quickly before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，天色很快就暗了下来。
senses.why: Speed in time is also speed of change, so quickly can mark how soon a new state appears.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的快也是变化上的快，所以 quickly 可以标记一种新状态出现得有多早。

senses.title: With a fast mind
senses.definition: in a way that shows fast thinking or fast noticing
senses.definitionCN: 以显出思维或察觉很快的方式
senses.example: She quickly saw what the problem was.
senses.exampleCN: 她很快就看出问题出在哪里。
senses.why: The adjective also described a lively mind, and the adverb carries that mental sense alongside physical speed.
senses.whyCN: 形容词也形容头脑灵活，副词就把这层心智义与身体的速度义一起带上。

intro.en: Quickly is the adjective quick with the English manner suffix -ly; its history is the history of quick itself.
intro.cn: quickly 是形容词 quick 加上英语方式词尾 -ly；它的历史就是 quick 本身的历史。

items.en: The root cwic meant alive, and it is the source of the whole family.
items.cn: 词根 cwic 意为活着的，是整族词的源头。

items.en: Quick moved from alive to lively and then to fast, and adverbs of manner were formed from it.
items.cn: quick 从「活着」走到「活跃」，再到「快」，方式副词也就由它构成。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb, naming the manner in which something is done.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变成副词，指出做某事的方式。

items.en: Quickly settled as the standard adverb of speed, beside the older phrase in quick time.
items.cn: quickly 固定为表示速度的标准副词，与较早的说法 in quick time 并存。

items.en: Modern English uses quickly for physical speed, for short delay and for mental alertness.
items.cn: 现代英语用 quickly 指身体速度、短暂延迟与心智的机敏。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective and its relatives; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of speed and promptness.
note.cn: 形近组收形容词及其亲属形式；近义组收表示速度与及时性的副词。

entries.definition: Fast, brief or easily angered.
To make or become faster.
The quality of being fast.
Loose sand that swallows what stands on it.
entries.definitionCN: 会吞没立足之物的流沙。

entries.definition: At a very fast rate.
Smoothly and at speed.
Without any delay.
At high speed, often of movement.

normalIntro.en: The word is the plain adverb of quick; every sense follows from the idea of little time being used.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 quick 的普通副词；每一层意思都从「只用了很少时间」这一想法引出。

normal.en: Quickly is quick plus -ly, and the suffix simply tells you that the word now describes how something is done.
normal.cn: quickly 就是 quick 加 -ly，这个后缀只是告诉你，这个词现在描述事情是怎样做的。

normal.en: More quickly and most quickly are the comparatives, because a two-syllable adverb prefers more over -er.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more quickly 与 most quickly，因为双音节副词更倾向用 more 而不用 -er。

normal.en: As quickly as possible is the standard phrase for doing something at the greatest safe speed.
normal.cn: as quickly as possible 是做某事时「在安全前提下尽快」的标准说法。

normal.en: Quickly can describe a mind as well as a body, as in she quickly saw the point.
normal.cn: quickly 既能描述身体也能描述头脑，如她很快抓住了要点。

normal.en: Placed at the start of a sentence, quickly often signals that the next event followed at once.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，quickly 常常表示紧接着就发生了下一件事。

abstract.en: An adverb of speed quietly tells us what the speaker values: some things should be done quickly, others never.
abstract.cn: 一个表示速度的副词悄悄透露了说话者的价值判断：有些事应当尽快做，有些则永远不该。

abstract.en: Quickly and well are often set against each other, though the best work sometimes manages both.
abstract.cn: 快与好常被摆在对立面，尽管最好的工作有时两者兼得。

abstract.en: To say that something happened quickly is also to say that there was little time to notice it happening.
abstract.cn: 说某事发生得快，也等于说几乎没留下让人察觉它的时间。

examples.en: He quickly shut the window when the rain started.
examples.cn: 雨一开始下，他就迅速关上了窗。

examples.en: The rumour spread quickly through the small town.
examples.cn: 谣言很快传遍了这座小镇。

examples.en: She quickly realized that the address was wrong.
examples.cn: 她很快意识到地址写错了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快克力」——像快克力一样一触即发，动作瞬间完成，记住 quickly 是迅速地。

root: 古英语 cwic（活着的）→ quick（快的）+ 英语副词词尾 -ly → quickly；同族有 quick、quicken、quickness。

sensesIntro.en: The core is little time taken; the senses divide into physical speed, short delay and fast thinking.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「用的时间少」；义项分为身体的速度、短暂的延迟与快速的思维。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second hand sweeping past marks almost too fast to read.
core.cn: 核心意象：秒针扫过刻度，快得几乎读不出来。

branches.en: a pot lifted before the water spills
branches.cn: 在水溢出前把锅端起

branches.en: a sky turning grey in minutes
branches.cn: 几分钟内转灰的天空

branches.en: a problem understood at a glance
branches.cn: 一眼就看懂的问题

branches.en: the same short span of time seen from outside and from inside
branches.cn: 同一段短促时间，从外面看与从里面看

branches.en: a fast hand guided by a fast eye
branches.cn: 被快眼引导的快手

intro.en: The word is the old adjective of speed with the most common English adverb ending, so its structure is root plus manner suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示速度的古老形容词加上最常见的英语副词词尾，结构就是词根加方式后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 锁；锁具；锁上；卡住；一绺头发；船闸
definition_en: to fasten something with a key or a catch, or the fastening device itself, a strand of hair, or a canal gate
core_image: 钥匙一转，锁舌滑进扣槽，门与门框从此扣成一体
scene: 夜里的院门半掩着，她伸手把铁锁扣好才上楼。 She locked the gate and checked it twice before leaving.
sceneCN: 这里是「锁上、用锁锁住」（第 1 个义项：用钥匙或扣件把门关牢）；句意为她把院门锁好，走前还检查了两遍。可辨物件：院门、铁锁、楼道灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 lock 加表示相反动作的前缀 un- 构成，义为「开锁」
由 pad 与 lock 复合而成，义为「挂锁」
由 lock 与表示工匠的 smith 复合而成，义为「锁匠」
由 lock 加表示容器的后缀 -er 构成，义为「带锁的储物柜」

senses.title: To fasten something with a lock
senses.definition: to close and secure a door, box or vehicle with a key or a catch so that it cannot be opened easily
senses.definitionCN: 用钥匙或扣件把门、箱子或车辆关紧，使别人不容易打开
senses.example: She locked the door and put the key in her pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 她锁上门，把钥匙放进口袋。
senses.why: The Old English noun loc named the fastening itself, and the verb grew out of the act of turning that fastening shut.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词 loc 本指扣件本身，动词义就是从「把这扣件扣上」这个动作长出来的。

senses.title: To become stuck and unable to move
senses.definition: to become fixed in one position, so that a part cannot turn or move freely
senses.definitionCN: 固定在某个位置，使某个部件无法转动或自由活动
senses.example: The wheels locked when he hit the brake hard.
senses.exampleCN: 他猛踩刹车时车轮抱死了。
senses.why: Once a lock is shut, nothing moves through it; applied to machines, the same image means a part that will not turn.
senses.whyCN: 锁一旦扣上，什么东西都过不去；用在机械上，同一个意象就指再也转不动的部件。

senses.title: The fastening device itself
senses.definition: a device with a key, a dial or a code that keeps a door or container shut
senses.definitionCN: 用钥匙、转盘或密码让门或容器保持关闭的装置
senses.example: The old trunk had a heavy brass lock.
senses.exampleCN: 这只旧箱子配着一把沉重的黄铜锁。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, the thing you hold in your hand, and every other sense spreads out from it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，即你手里握着的那个物件，其余义项都从它扩散出去。

senses.title: A strand or small bunch of hair
senses.definition: a small quantity of hair that hangs or grows together as one piece
senses.definitionCN: 共同垂下或长在一起的一小束头发
senses.example: A lock of hair fell across her forehead.
senses.exampleCN: 一绺头发垂落在她额前。
senses.why: Hair that holds together in one clump looks like something fastened, so the word for a fastening was reused for a bunch of hair.
senses.whyCN: 头发聚成一束，看起来就像被扣住的东西，于是表示扣件的词又被用来指一束头发。

senses.title: A section of a canal with gates
senses.definition: a part of a canal closed off by gates, where the water level is raised or lowered for boats
senses.definitionCN: 运河上用闸门隔出的一段，通过升降水位让船只通过
senses.example: The barge waited for the lock to fill with water.
senses.exampleCN: 驳船等着船闸注满水。
senses.why: A canal lock works by shutting water in or out, which is exactly what a lock does to a door.
senses.whyCN: 船闸靠把水关进或放出而工作，这正是锁对门所做的那件事。

intro.en: Lock is a native English word whose deeper Germanic origin is reconstructed rather than recorded, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: lock 是英语本土词，更早的日耳曼语来源属于重构而非有记录的原形，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The fastening is generally traced to a Germanic root luk-, whose exact shape is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 这类扣件一般认为可追到日耳曼语词根 luk-，其确切形式属于重构，而不是有记录的原形。

items.en: Old English loc meant a fastening, a bolt or a barrier, and it also named a lock of hair.
items.cn: 古英语 loc 指扣件、门闩或障碍，同时也指一绺头发。

items.en: Middle English lock kept both the device and the hair sense, and the verb locken appeared for shutting something with it.
items.cn: 中古英语 lock 同时保留器具与头发两个义项，动词 locken 出现，表示用锁具关住。

items.en: Modern English added canal locks, and the verb widened to mean any part that jams and will not move.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了船闸义，动词也扩展到指任何卡住不动的部件。

items.en: Today the word covers keys and doors, traffic queues, canal gates, and a single strand of hair.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖钥匙与门、排队的车辆、船闸闸门以及一束头发。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on lock or closely spelled compounds; the near-meaning group collects fastening devices and the act of fastening.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lock 构成或拼写相近的复合词；近义组收各类扣件以及「扣紧」这个动作。

entries.definition: To open something that was locked.
A small lock with a movable hoop, used on gates and bags.
entries.definitionCN: 带活动环扣的小锁，用于门和包上。

entries.definition: A person who makes and repairs locks.
A small cupboard that can be locked, used for storage.
entries.definitionCN: 可上锁的小柜子，用于存放物品。

entries.definition: A small bar that keeps a door or gate closed.
entries.definitionCN: 让门或栅栏保持关闭的小闩。

entries.definition: A sliding bar used to fasten a door.
To attach or close something firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定或关紧。

entries.definition: A small device that holds two parts together.
entries.definitionCN: 把两部分扣在一起的小扣件。

normalIntro.en: Lock is an Old English word for a fastening, and its many senses all come from one picture: something held shut.
normalIntro.cn: lock 是古英语中表示扣件的词，它的众多义项都出自同一个画面：某样东西被扣住不放。

normal.en: Lock is an Old English word for a fastening, older than any Latin borrowing in this entry.
normal.cn: lock 是古英语中表示扣件的词，比这条词条里的任何拉丁借词都古老。

normal.en: Unlock is simply un- plus lock, the prefix undoing the fastening.
normal.cn: unlock 就是 un- 加 lock，前缀把扣紧的状态解掉。

normal.en: A lock of hair is not a different word: hair that holds together looks fastened.
normal.cn: a lock of hair 并不是另一个词：头发聚成一束，看起来像被扣住了。

normal.en: Lock up, lock in and lock out all keep the same core of shutting something in or out.
normal.cn: lock up、lock in 与 lock out 都保留着「把东西关进或关外」这同一个核心。

normal.en: A canal lock locks water in or out, which is why the same word serves boats and doors.
normal.cn: 船闸把水关进或放出，所以同一个词能同时用于船和门。

abstract.en: A lock is a promise made in metal: only the right person passes.
abstract.cn: 锁是用金属做出的承诺：只有对的人才能通过。

abstract.en: When a wheel locks, the machine briefly behaves like a shut door.
abstract.cn: 车轮抱死时，机器短暂地像一扇关上的门。

abstract.en: The word joins a keyhole, a hair strand and a canal gate because all three are things that hold together or shut.
abstract.cn: 这个词把钥匙孔、一束头发和闸门连在一起，因为三者都是「扣住」或「关住」的东西。

examples.en: Remember to lock the back door before you leave.
examples.cn: 走之前记得把后门锁上。

examples.en: A thick lock of hair fell over her eyes.
examples.cn: 厚厚一绺头发垂到她眼睛上。

examples.en: The ship waited for the lock gates to open.
examples.cn: 船等着闸门打开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「落扣」——门一关，锁舌落进扣槽，咔一声就锁住了；记住 lock 是锁。

root: 古英语 loc（扣件、门闩，也指一束头发），一般认为与日耳曼语中表示「关闭、扣住」的词根有关，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something held shut; the senses then spread from the device to its action, to a jammed part, to a clump of hair and to a canal gate.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被扣住不放」；义项由器具扩散到动作、卡死的部件、一束头发，以及运河闸门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key turns, the bolt slides into its slot, and door and frame become one closed piece.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙一转，锁舌滑进扣槽，门与门框扣成一体。

branches.en: a key turning twice in a gate at night
branches.cn: 夜里钥匙在院门上转了两圈

branches.en: brake pads gripping a wheel that will not turn
branches.cn: 刹车片咬住再也转不动的车轮

branches.en: a brass lock hanging on an old trunk
branches.cn: 一只旧箱子上挂着的黄铜锁

branches.en: a strand of hair falling over one eye
branches.cn: 垂到一只眼睛前的一绺头发

branches.en: a barge rising slowly inside a canal lock
branches.cn: 驳船在船闸里缓缓上升

intro.en: Lock is a native English word, so its parts are Old English forms plus modern prefixes and compounds rather than Latin pieces.
intro.cn: lock 是英语本土词，所以它的各部分由古英语形式加上现代前缀与复合成分组成，而不是拉丁语构件。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it is a native Germanic word, so the Latin column stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它是本土的日耳曼语词，因此拉丁同族一栏留空。

definition_zh: 板；木板；董事会；登（船、机）；膳宿
definition_en: a flat piece of wood used for building, a group that governs a company, or to get on a ship, train or plane
core_image: 几块长条木板并排钉成的桌面
scene: 木工房里，师傅把两块长木板并排钉在一起，做成一扇门。 The carpenter nailed two boards together to make a door.
sceneCN: 这里 board 是「木板」（第 1 个义项：平整的木料）；句意为木匠把两块木板钉在一起做成一扇门。

pos.zh: 名词：板；木板；董事会；膳食

derivatives.zh: 由 a- 与 board 构成，义为「在船（或飞机）上」
由 board 加 -er 构成，义为「寄宿生；房客」
由 board 加 -ing 构成，义为「登乘；寄宿」
由 key 与 board 组合而成，义为「键盘」

senses.title: A flat piece of wood
senses.definition: a long thin flat piece of wood or similar material used in building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑用的长而薄的平整木料或类似材料
senses.example: He nailed two boards together.
senses.exampleCN: 他把两块木板钉在一起。
senses.why: Old English bord meant a plank, and that flat piece of timber is still the plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bord 指一块木板，这种平整的木材仍是最朴素的义项。

senses.title: A governing group
senses.definition: a group of people who manage or direct a company or organization
senses.definitionCN: 管理或领导公司、机构的一组人
senses.example: The board approved the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会批准了新方案。
senses.why: Such groups once met around a long table, and the table itself was called a board, so the people took the name.
senses.whyCN: 这类人过去围着一张长桌开会，而桌子本身就叫 board，于是这些人也得了这个名字。

senses.title: To get on a vehicle
senses.definition: to get onto a ship, train, plane or bus
senses.definitionCN: 走上船、火车、飞机或公交车
senses.example: We boarded the train at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们中午登上了火车。
senses.why: Getting onto a ship once meant stepping onto its wooden boards, and the verb kept that picture.
senses.whyCN: 上船过去意味着踏上山船的木板，这个动词保留的就是那幅画面。

senses.title: Meals and lodging
senses.definition: food and a place to sleep, usually provided for payment
senses.definitionCN: 饭菜与住处，通常付费提供
senses.example: The job offers free room and board.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作提供免费食宿。
senses.why: Meals were served on a board, so board came to mean the food a person is given.
senses.whyCN: 饭菜端在桌上，于是 board 引申为供给一个人的伙食。

intro.en: Board began as a plank, and the table made from planks gave it the senses of meals and of the people who meet there.
intro.cn: board 最初指一块木板，而用木板做成的桌子又给出「伙食」和「围桌开会的人」两个义项。

items.en: Old English bord meant a plank or a flat board used in building and in ships.
items.cn: 古英语 bord 指建筑和船上使用的木板或平板。

items.en: Dutch bord and German Brett are relatives, all naming a flat piece of wood.
items.cn: 荷兰语 bord 与德语 Brett 是同源词，都指一块平整的木头。

items.en: A board set on legs became a table, and meals served on it were also called board.
items.cn: 架起腿的木板成了桌子，摆在上面的饭菜也被称作 board。

items.en: Because a council met around one table, its members were called the board.
items.cn: 由于委员会围着一张桌子开会，成员们就被称作 the board。

items.en: To go aboard a ship was to step onto its boards, which gave the verb its travel sense.
items.cn: 上船就是踩上船板，这给出动词表示「登上」的义项。

items.en: Today board covers timber, a governing group, meals and the act of getting on a vehicle.
items.cn: 今天 board 覆盖木料、管理机构、伙食以及登上交通工具的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape or sound; the near-meaning group collects words for planks and committees.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音接近的词；近义组收表示木板与委员会的词。

entries.definition: The past form of bore, meaning tired and uninterested.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「感到无聊的」，与 board 同音。

entries.definition: Wide from side to side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽阔的」，拼写与 board 相近。

entries.definition: To talk too proudly about what one has done.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吹嘘」，拼写与 board 相近。

entries.definition: A long thick piece of sawn wood.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「厚木板」，对应 board 的木料义。

entries.definition: A group chosen to decide or manage something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「委员会」，对应 board 的管理群体义。

entries.definition: A flat piece of material, or a small group of experts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「板；专家小组」，兼有 board 的两层意思。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English bord meant a plank, and that flat timber is still the first sense.
normal.cn: 古英语 bord 指木板，这种平整的木料仍是第一个义项。

normal.en: A board on legs became a table, so meals served there were also called board.
normal.cn: 架起腿的木板成了桌子，摆在上面的饭菜也被称作 board。

normal.en: A council met around one table, which is why its members are the board.
normal.cn: 委员会围着一张桌子开会，所以成员们就被称作 the board。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with on board, room, directors and game.
normal.cn: 它常与 on board、room、directors、game 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-o-a-r-d; the oa sounds like the o in more.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-a-r-d，中间的 oa 读得像 more 里的 o。

abstract.en: See several long planks laid side by side: that flat surface is board.
abstract.cn: 想象几块长木板并排铺开：那个平面就是 board。

abstract.en: Put legs under the planks and people sit around it to eat and decide.
abstract.cn: 在木板下装上腿，人们就围着它吃饭和决定事情。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the planks bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那些木板把意思带回来。

examples.en: He nailed two boards together.
examples.cn: 他把两块木板钉在一起。

examples.en: The board approved the new plan.
examples.cn: 董事会批准了新方案。

examples.en: We boarded the train at noon.

root: board 来自古英语 bord，指建筑与船上使用的木板，荷兰语 bord 与德语 Brett 是同源词。架起腿的木板成了桌子，摆在桌上的饭菜也被称作 board；委员会围桌开会，成员便成了 the board。上船原本是踩上船板，于是动词有了「登上」的意思。今天它覆盖木料、管理机构、伙食与登乘动作。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of board rest on one picture: a flat plank, and the table, meals and meetings that planks made possible.

branches.cn: 船线：踩上船的木板，就是 boarding。

branches.en: THE MEAL: food served on the table is also called board.
branches.cn: 伙食线：端上桌的饭菜也被称作 board。

branches.en: THE TABLE: the same table links the council and the meals.
branches.cn: 桌子线：同一张桌子把委员会与伙食连在一起。

definition_zh: 生日；诞辰；生日聚会
definition_en: the day each year when a person was born, or the celebration held on that day
core_image: 插着蜡烛的蛋糕，桌上散着彩纸和礼物
scene: 晚饭后，家人关掉灯，把插着蜡烛的蛋糕端上桌。 My birthday is in June.
sceneCN: 这里 birthday 是「生日」（第 1 个义项：每年出生的那个日子）；句意为我的生日在六月。

pos.zh: 名词：生日；诞辰；生日聚会

口语说法，字面为「生日礼服」，实指赤裸的身体

senses.title: The yearly date of birth
senses.definition: the day of the year on which a person was born, remembered each year
senses.definitionCN: 一年中某人出生的那个日子，每年都会纪念
senses.example: My birthday is in June.
senses.exampleCN: 我的生日在六月。
senses.why: The word simply joins birth with day, so it first names the calendar date on which someone was born.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只是把 birth 与 day 合在一起，所以它首先指某人出生在日历上的那一天。

senses.title: The celebration
senses.definition: a party or celebration held to mark a birthday
senses.definitionCN: 为庆祝生日而举办的聚会或庆祝活动
senses.example: We are going to a birthday on Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 周六我们要去参加一个生日聚会。
senses.why: In casual speech the day and the party held on it share one word, so going to a birthday means going to the celebration.
senses.whyCN: 在口语里，这一天和为它办的聚会被同一个词覆盖，所以说去一个 birthday 就是去参加庆祝会。

senses.title: The founding date of a group
senses.definition: the yearly date on which an important person or organization was founded
senses.definitionCN: 重要人物或机构每年被纪念的诞生或成立之日
senses.example: The school celebrated its hundredth birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校庆祝了它的百岁诞辰。
senses.why: Schools and nations are pictured as living things that were born on a date, so birthday also marks their founding anniversary.
senses.whyCN: 学校与国家被当作在某天诞生的生命体，所以 birthday 也用来标记它们的成立纪念日。

intro.en: Birthday is a plain English compound of birth and day, and its party sense is much newer.
intro.cn: birthday 是 birth 与 day 组成的朴素英语复合词，而「聚会」义要晚得多。

items.en: Old English byrddaeg joined gebyrd, birth, with daeg, day.
items.cn: 古英语 byrddaeg 把 gebyrd「出生」与 daeg「日子」合在一起。

items.en: The compound survived with the shortened first element birth, matching the noun birth.
items.cn: 这一复合词保留下来，第一个成分缩短为 birth，与名词 birth 一致。

items.en: Birthday cakes and candles spread in the nineteenth century and made the day a family occasion.
items.cn: 生日蛋糕与蜡烛在十九世纪流行开来，使这一天成为家庭节日。

items.en: In modern speech a birthday can also name the party held on that day, as in going to a birthday.
items.cn: 现代口语里，birthday 也可指当天举办的聚会，如 go to a birthday。

items.en: The word spread to the founding day of schools, cities, and nations.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到了学校、城市与国家的成立纪念日。

definition_zh: 需要；要求；规定
definition_en: to need something, or to demand it as a rule or condition
core_image: 一张任务清单上，某些条件被画了红圈，缺一项就无法开工
scene: 这份工作需要耐心和稳定的手，体检合格是硬性条件。 The job requires patience and careful hands.
sceneCN: 这里 require 是「需要」（第 1 个义项：某事成功所不可缺少的条件）；句意：这份工作需要耐心和一双稳当的手。

derivatives.zh: 要求；必要条件
必需的
征用；申请单

senses.title: To need something
senses.definition: to need something in order to happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 为了发生或成功而不可缺少某物
senses.example: This plant requires plenty of sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物需要充足的阳光。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to seek again, and a need is something the situation keeps seeking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「再次寻求」，而「需要」正是情境不断寻求的东西。

senses.title: To demand by rule
senses.definition: to officially demand something as a rule or condition
senses.definitionCN: 以规则或条件的形式正式要求某事
senses.example: The law requires drivers to carry a licence.
senses.exampleCN: 法律要求司机携带驾照。
senses.why: An authority can turn a need into an obligation, which gives the word its demanding sense.
senses.whyCN: 权威可以把「需要」变成义务，于是这个词带上了强制要求的意味。

senses.title: To make necessary
senses.definition: to make something necessary as a result or consequence
senses.definitionCN: 作为结果或后果使某事成为必要
senses.example: The repair will require closing the road.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修将需要封闭道路。
senses.why: If a condition cannot be met without an action, the condition effectively requires the action.
senses.whyCN: 如果缺少某个行动就无法满足条件，这个条件实际上就「要求」了该行动。

intro.en: Require comes from Latin requirere, to seek again, built from re- and quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: require 来自拉丁语 requirere（再次寻求），由 re- 与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问或探问。

items.en: Requirere adds re- and means to look for something, especially something missing.
items.cn: requirere 加上 re-，意为寻找某物，尤指缺失之物。

items.en: The verb develops the sense of needing what is sought.
items.cn: 该动词发展出「需要所寻之物」的意思。

items.en: Old French requerre carries the demand sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 requerre 把「要求」义带入英语。

items.en: Middle English require covers need, demand, and obligation.
items.cn: 中古英语 require 涵盖需要、要求和义务。

items.en: Modern English uses it for rules, conditions, and logical consequences.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表示规则、条件和逻辑后果。

note.en: Require shares its seeking root with request, and its family includes the noun for a condition and the word for something indispensable.
note.cn: require 与 request 共享「寻求」词根，其词族包括表示条件的名词和表示不可或缺之物的词。

normal.en: Re- means again, and quire sounds like quest: keep seeking until the need is met.

normal.en: Require attention means attention is not optional.
normal.cn: require attention 意为关注不是可选项。

normal.en: Require sb to do is the pattern for rules that force an action.
normal.cn: require sb to do 是强制行动的规则句型。

normal.en: As required is the phrase for doing something when a rule says so.
normal.cn: as required 意为「按规则要求去做」。

normal.en: Compare request and require: asking politely versus demanding by need or rule.
normal.cn: 对比 request 与 require：礼貌询问与因需要或规则而要求。

abstract.cn: 想象清单上几个不能跳过的项目被红笔圈出。

abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，必须满足三个条件才会打开。

abstract.cn: 想象一份食谱，少一样材料就会失败。

examples.cn: 这份工作需要很强的沟通能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（再次）+ quire（寻求）＝不断寻求、必须有，即需要或要求；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ quaerere（寻求）→ requirere（寻找、索取）→ 古法语 requerre → 中古英语 require。

sensesIntro.en: A need comes first, then a rule that turns the need into an obligation, then the consequence that makes an action necessary.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是需要，再是把需要变成义务的规则，最后是使某个行动成为必要的后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a condition circled in red that must be met before anything proceeds.

branches.en: The plain need is the basic sense of the verb.

branches.en: A rule turns the need into an official demand.

branches.en: A consequence can make an action necessary.

branches.en: Need and demand both point to something that cannot be skipped.

senses.title: Quality sensed by the nose
senses.definition: the quality of something that you notice with your nose

senses.title: Notice with the nose

definition_zh: 当然；肯定地；无疑地
definition_en: surely; without doubt; used to agree or emphasize
core_image: 响亮地点头：这件事一秒钟也不用怀疑
scene: 同学问我能不能借他一把伞，我笑着答应了。 You can certainly borrow my umbrella for the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 certainly 是「当然」（第 1 个义项：用于爽快答应）；句意是我爽快地答应借伞给同学。

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词基础，义为「确定的」

senses.title: A strong yes; of course
senses.definition: used to say yes in a friendly, confident way
senses.definitionCN: 以友好而自信的方式表示同意
senses.example: May I open the window? Certainly.
senses.exampleCN: 我能开窗吗？当然可以。
senses.why: Agreement given with full sureness sounds warm and strong.
senses.whyCN: 带着十足的把握去答应，听起来热情有力。

senses.title: Without doubt; surely
senses.definition: used to emphasize that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 强调某事属实或必将发生
senses.example: He will certainly pass the exam this time.
senses.exampleCN: 这次他肯定会通过考试。
senses.why: The sentence leans on the word to remove all doubt.
senses.whyCN: 句子借这个词扫清一切疑虑。

senses.title: Emphasis in a surprising statement
senses.definition: used to admit a point before adding another view
senses.definitionCN: 先承认某点再补充看法
senses.example: The trip was tiring, but certainly worth it.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行很累，但确实值得。
senses.why: Speakers use it to hold one idea steady while adding another.
senses.whyCN: 说话者用它稳住一个观点，再补上另一层意思。
